claims.claim: Published crop assemblages support persistence of crop groups with changing proportions
claims.status: source-reported observation and prior bounded calculation
claims.limit: No direct measure of teaching, political organization, landholding or language

claims.claim: Local recurring work and specialists transmitted some practical knowledge through urban change
claims.limit: Source observations motivate the carrier but do not identify a historical transmission chain

claims.claim: Sanskrit is Indo-Aryan within Indo-Iranian, with a shared linguistic history with Iranian languages
claims.limit: No language assignment to an Indus inscription follows

claims.claim: The Rigvedic ploughing passage supplies agricultural vocabulary and ritual representation
claims.limit: Generic operations and a family-book location do not authenticate a Harappan predecessor or an earliest text layer

claims.claim: Horsegram names provide a published candidate for knowledge transmission across Dravidian, Indo-Aryan and Munda languages
claims.limit: The lexical borrowing direction and date need independent testing; the paper also supports separate domestication trajectories

claims.claim: Population mixture and alternative ancestry proxies are compatible with composite cultural histories
claims.limit: Both Dravidian scenarios retained in N2019; genetic proxies do not uniquely identify an archaeological culture or a language

claims.claim: Later Vedic institutions assembled older traditions into changed ritual systems
claims.limit: No specific Indus ritual lineage established

claims.claim: Regional agricultural contact contributed knowledge to early Indo-Aryan communities
claims.limit: Supported borrowing must be distinguished from inheritance, innovation and unknown etymology

claims.claim: A diagnostic Vedic farming operation has an Indus-period regional ancestor
claims.limit: No diagnostic bundle or dated cross-domain chain currently passes the required test

claims.claim: Middle Indo-Aryan varieties developed alongside the continuing use of Sanskrit
claims.limit: Classical Sanskrit is not a simple intermediate parent for all later spoken varieties
